about: The jsdom-parity gap ledger (Phase 0 of the parity plan). Generated from scripts/surface-diff.mjs and scripts/area-diff.mjs against the oracle below; groups are classified by hand because the raw member counts repeat the same systematic gaps on every interface. scripts/check-gaps.mjs re-runs the surface inventory and fails if the recorded surface facts drift. Semantic area scores are snapshots with their run parameters; they change only when the generators or the engine change, and Phase 2 drives them to full agreement (or to an adjudicated note, where jsdom itself departs from the spec).
outOfScope: Layout values (getBoundingClientRect and friends return 0) — README non-goal
Canvas, iframe contents, real WebSocket/EventSource/Worker transports, media decoding — README non-goals
jsdom's 29 underscore-prefixed window internals — not public API (design doc section 1)

findings.what: At-target invocation order of listeners with mixed capture flags differs (jsdom fired a later-registered listener first in one trace). Reduce and adjudicate against the spec in Phase 2.
The onclick IDL handler fires before addEventListener listeners in jsdom, in registration order in ours. Adjudicate against the spec/browser in Phase 2 before choosing a side.

compareBoundaryPoints: jsdom throws WrongDocumentError when the boundary points sit in detached or different subtrees; ours returns a number (closer to browsers). Adjudicate in Phase 2; more findings expected as divergent programs are reduced.
select.selectedIndex = -1 does not deselect all options (ours keeps index 0).
input[type=number].value accepts non-numeric strings ('abc' is kept); jsdom sanitises to '' and validity follows.
form.reset() does not restore default values or default selectedness (input values and the select stay where the program left them).

The systematic divergences are jsdom's computed style being poorer: it returns '' for width/opacity/font-size initial values and leaves var() unresolved, where ours resolves (width: auto/7px, opacity: 1, font-size: 16px). This area's oracle is the spec and browsers, not jsdom; do not 'fix' toward jsdom. Real gaps, if any, surface only against a browser reference.

Misnested formatting elements are not reconstructed: xy parses to xy in ours, xy in jsdom (parse5, the spec's adoption agency algorithm). The htmlparser2 port omits it. More tree-construction gaps (foster parenting, active formatting elements) are expected; enumerate per corpus entry in Phase 2.

semantic.run: scripts/area-diff.mjs, 20 programs x 60 steps per area

groups.what: The aria* IDL reflection properties (ariaAtomic, ariaBusy, ariaChecked, ...) are absent from Element instances; the attributes themselves work.

Six legacy Node constants (ATTRIBUTE_NODE, CDATA_SECTION_NODE, ENTITY_NODE, ENTITY_REFERENCE_NODE, NOTATION_NODE, PROCESSING_INSTRUCTION_NODE) are absent from instance prototype chains; the common constants (ELEMENT_NODE, TEXT_NODE, the DOCUMENT_POSITION_* set) are present.
The window on* handler properties (onclick, onload, ...) are not globals. Element-level on* IDL handlers do work (see the events area).

The class is not exposed as a window global, while objects of it are reachable and work (classList, dataset, MutationObserver records, location/history/navigator were all measured live). instanceof checks and name lookups fail.
Genuinely absent interfaces and window functions.

CSSStyleDeclaration carries jsdom's whole CSS property database as member names (every longhand and -webkit-* alias). Ours exposes far fewer names. Distinct from computed-style behaviour, which the style area covers.
Text: splitText and wholeText are absent; CharacterData lacks nextElementSibling/previousElementSibling; Text lacks assignedSlot.
Legacy Document members (anchors, applets, captureEvents, clear, releaseEvents, ...) are absent.

In prototype-chain walks, attributes/options/rows/childNodes objects did not show the NamedNodeMap/HTMLCollection prototype members (item, namedItem, getNamedItemNS). This may be an enumeration artefact of how the guest materialises live collections. Verify on live objects before counting it as a gap — first task of Phase 1.
